blocks.text: Show that you can keep the feed smooth under heavy load. Optimize rendering, media, and update frequency.

blocks.title: Performance techniques
items: Keep rendering bounded; add list windowing only when representative measurements justify it.
Retain accepted events and coalesce visible projection updates at a measured cadence.
Lazy-load media and use placeholders to avoid layout shifts.
Memoize row components to reduce re-rendering.
Prefetch the next page when near the end.
Schedule deferrable work during measured idle periods only when the platform capability and product priority permit it.

blocks.title: Common bottlenecks and fixes
rows: Reduce row complexity; add measured windowing if DOM cost remains high
Accept only a newer server-authoritative FeedOrder revision

items.label: Mounted content
items.helperText: Window only when DOM and layout evidence justify it.

items.label: Projection cadence

blocks.title: High-risk pitfall
blocks.text: Do not insert items above the viewport without anchoring; it will shift scroll position and feel broken. Use a banner or scroll anchoring APIs.

blocks.title: Observability
items: Track CLS, INP, and long tasks during scroll.
Log dedupe rate and buffer size to detect stream bursts.

blocks.title: Failure modes
rows: Deduplicate without reordering committed earlier pages.
Choose the nearest surviving neighbor and explain major filter changes.
Keep text, dimensions, and controls with a fallback.
One asset does not collapse the card.
Mark live freshness and request snapshot repair.

blocks.text: Use a feed or semantic list with named articles and a visible Load More path. New ranked or live items never steal focus or auto-scroll a reader. Media has appropriate alternatives, reaction controls expose state, and grouped loading or new-item status avoids a stream of announcements. Windowing must preserve reachable focus and article context.

Prove paging, deduplication, and anchor restoration before enabling live inserts or aggressive windowing. Test overlapping pages, rank revisions, removed anchors, media failures, offline retry, mobile layout, keyboard navigation, and long sessions. Track jumps, duplicate IDs, missing pages, and recovery.

Prioritize text and geometry for the first useful cards, then schedule media from viewport direction and connection evidence. Reserve image aspect ratios, cancel obsolete preloads, and cap decoded resources. Measure mounted DOM, layout work, memory, and focus behavior before adding windowing. When windowing is justified, keep the anchor and focused article mounted until a safe handoff, and test variable-height corrections caused by translated text, media, and moderation changes.

Cache isolation includes account, locale, filters, and experiment assignment when they affect content. Signing out clears personal feed state. Telemetry records cursor, rank revision, merge outcome, gap, layout shift, and user-visible recovery without copying post bodies. Rollout can separate new rank projection, live buffering, media policy, and windowing behind independent flags so a scroll-jump regression does not require disabling basic pagination.

blocks.title: news feed timeline answer rubric
items: Must — Merge cursor pages and live updates by stable identity under a server-authoritative rank revision.
Must — Preserve the reading anchor while keeping rendering work bounded on representative devices.
Strong signal — Buffer disruptive inserts behind a new-items affordance instead of moving the viewport.
Strong signal — Reserve media geometry and accept pagination only for the active query generation.
Expert stretch — Add list windowing only when measurements justify its accessibility and restoration cost.
Red flag — Re-sorting ranked posts by client timestamps or assuming virtualization is a requirement.
